chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Malik ibn Atiyya from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that in...

what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O Musa ibn Imran! I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than My believing servant. Indeed, I test him for what is better for him, and I grant him health for what is better for him, and I turn away from him what is evil for him for what is better for him, and I am more Knowing of what suits My servant. So let him be patient with My afflictions, and let him be grateful for My bounties, and let him be pleased with My judgement. I shall record him among the truthful ones in My Presence when he acts by My pleasure and obeys My command.'
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind Allah testing believers according to the Hadith of Musa?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the divine wisdom behind trials (balā’) and blessings (ni‘am), framing them as acts of mercy from a God who knows best what is suitable for His servants. It underscores the Shia emphasis on sabr (patience) and shukr (gratitude) as complementary virtues that lead to the high spiritual station of al-Siddiqin (the truthful). The text serves as a theological foundation for understanding divine decree (qadā’) not as arbitrary fate, but as a purposeful mechanism for spiritual refinement and ultimate good.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Dawood Bin Farqad,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>:

‘Among what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa Bin Imran<sup>as</sup> was: “O Musa<sup>as</sup> Bin Imran! I<sup>azwj</sup> have not Created a creature more Beloved to Me<sup>azwj</sup> than My<sup>azwj</sup> believing servant. So I<sup>azwj</sup>, rather, Test him for what is better for him, and Grant him health which is better for him, and Deter from him what is evil for him to what is better for him, and I<sup>azwj</sup> am more Knowing with what is correct upon My<sup>azwj</sup> servant. Therefore, let him be patient upon My<sup>azwj</sup> afflictions, and let him be grateful for My<sup>azwj</sup> Bounties, and let him be pleased with My<sup>azwj</sup> Judgement. I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Write for him to be among the truthful ones in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, when he acts by My<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure and obeys My<sup>azwj</sup> Commands’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn ‘Atiyah from Dawud ibn Farqad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Of the revelations that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent to Moses ibn ‘Imran was as follows: ‘O, Moses, son of ‘Imran, I have not created anything more beloved to Me than My believing servant. I try him only because it is for his good. I give him good health just for his good. I hold back what is evil for him in favor of what is for his good. I know best in what conditions My servant works for his own best interest. He then must bear patience in My trials, appreciate My favors and agree with My decision. I count him among the truthful ones before Me if he acts according to My pleasure and obeys My command.’”
